title: Determinants of Childhood Immunization Defaulting Among Caregivers Attending Primary Healthcare Facilities in Rural North-West Nigeria
background: Childhood immunization remains one of the most effective public health interventions for preventing vaccine-preventable diseases. Despite improvements in immunization coverage across Nigeria, several northern states continue to report suboptimal vaccination uptake and high rates of immunization defaulting. Factors such as vaccine hesitancy, poor healthcare access, low maternal education, cultural beliefs, insecurity, and health system constraints contribute to missed vaccination opportunities. Immunization defaulting increases the risk of disease outbreaks, childhood morbidity, and mortality. Understanding the specific factors influencing caregivers' adherence to vaccination schedules is essential for designing targeted interventions that improve vaccine completion rates. Evidence from rural communities remains limited despite their disproportionate burden of under-immunization. This study seeks to identify determinants of childhood immunization defaulting among caregivers attending primary healthcare facilities in rural North-West Nigeria and generate evidence to support context-specific immunization strategies.
objectives: Assess the prevalence of childhood immunization defaulting among caregivers attending selected primary healthcare facilities.
Determine caregiver-related factors associated with immunization defaulting.
Examine health system factors influencing adherence to vaccination schedules.
Evaluate the effect of geographical accessibility on immunization completion.
Identify predictors of immunization defaulting among caregivers.
researchQuestions: What is the prevalence of childhood immunization defaulting among caregivers in the study area?
Which caregiver characteristics are associated with immunization defaulting?
How do health system factors influence vaccination schedule adherence?
What is the effect of healthcare accessibility on immunization completion?
Which factors independently predict immunization defaulting?
hypotheses: There is no significant association between caregiver educational status and childhood immunization defaulting.
There is no significant relationship between distance to healthcare facilities and immunization completion.
There is no significant association between healthcare service quality and immunization defaulting.
methodology: A facility-based cross-sectional analytical study will be conducted among caregivers of children aged 12–23 months attending selected primary healthcare facilities. Multistage sampling will be used to recruit participants. Data will be collected using structured interviewer-administered questionnaires and immunization card reviews. Descriptive statistics will summarize immunization status, while chi-square tests and logistic regression analyses will identify factors associated with immunization defaulting. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05.
sampleSuggestion: 350 caregivers of children aged 12–23 months attending primary healthcare facilities

title: Prevalence and Predictors of Postpartum Depression Among Mothers Receiving Postnatal Care in Urban Secondary Hospitals in South-West Nigeria
background: Postpartum depression is a major public health concern affecting maternal wellbeing, infant development, and family functioning. In Nigeria, mental health disorders among women are often underdiagnosed due to stigma, poor awareness, and limited integration of mental health services into maternal healthcare. Rapid urbanization, economic pressures, inadequate social support, and pregnancy-related complications may increase vulnerability to postpartum depression among Nigerian mothers. Despite growing recognition of maternal mental health as a critical component of reproductive health, evidence on the prevalence and determinants of postpartum depression remains insufficient in many urban settings. Early identification of at-risk mothers can improve maternal outcomes and inform interventions integrated within routine postnatal care services. This study seeks to assess the prevalence and predictors of postpartum depression among mothers attending postnatal clinics in selected urban secondary hospitals in South-West Nigeria.

Data will be collected using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale and structured questionnaires. Descriptive statistics will determine prevalence, while bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses will identify predictors. Statistical significance will be established at p < 0.05.

Exposure to smoke from traditional cooking methods contributes to respiratory infections, chronic respiratory diseases, and adverse health outcomes among women and children who spend considerable time near cooking areas. Despite increasing awareness of environmental health risks, clean cooking technologies remain inaccessible to many households due to economic and infrastructural barriers. Understanding the relationship between household air pollution exposure and respiratory health outcomes is essential for informing interventions aimed at reducing disease burden. title: Factors Influencing Antenatal Care Initiation During the First Trimester Among Pregnant Women in Semi-Urban Communities of South-East Nigeria
background: Early initiation of antenatal care is essential for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes through timely detection and management of pregnancy-related complications. However, many pregnant women in Nigeria initiate antenatal care late despite national and international recommendations. Delayed booking limits opportunities for preventive interventions, health education, and risk screening. Socioeconomic status, educational attainment, cultural beliefs, healthcare accessibility, and quality of services may influence antenatal care utilization. Although several studies have examined antenatal attendance, evidence specifically addressing first-trimester initiation remains limited in many semi-urban settings. Understanding factors associated with early antenatal care utilization is important for designing interventions that improve maternal healthcare-seeking behaviour. title: Assessment of Climate Change-Related Heat Exposure and Its Impact on Occupational Health Among Outdoor Workers in Lagos State
background: Climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of heat-related events globally, with significant implications for occupational health. In Nigeria, outdoor workers such as construction laborers, traffic officers, street vendors, and agricultural workers are increasingly exposed to prolonged periods of extreme heat. Heat exposure can contribute to dehydration, heat stress, reduced productivity, cardiovascular strain, and other adverse health outcomes. Despite growing concerns about climate-related health risks, limited empirical evidence exists regarding occupational heat exposure among vulnerable worker populations in Nigeria. Understanding the magnitude of heat-related health challenges and associated risk factors is essential for developing workplace adaptation strategies and public health policies.
